label: Nationality discrimination in access to employment
definition: The law governing access to the labour market does not give EU workers equal treatment with nationals, for example by treating them as any other foreigner or reserving private sector posts for nationals.
exclusion_notes: Work permit, quota and residence requirements belong to RI-FMW-002; restrictions on public sector posts belong to RI-FMW-003; nationality conditions in social security laws belong to RI-FMW-009.
notes: Largest group: the same recommendation is repeated each year from 2020 to 2025. Private sector reservations are placed here rather than in RI-FMW-003; the analyst may prefer a separate issue.

label: Work permits, quotas and residence conditions applied to EU workers
definition: EU workers and their family members are subject to work permits, annual quotas, residence permits or unspecified conditions (for example for seasonal work) that must be lifted or settled by accession.
exclusion_notes: The general principle of non-discrimination and overall alignment of labour market access law belong to RI-FMW-001; posted workers' social security belongs to RI-FMW-008.
notes: Several items are the country's own description (reported view) in the screening report. MEC-02 rests on one item on seasonal work.

label: Public sector posts closed to EU citizens beyond the public authority exception
definition: EU citizens are barred from public sector posts other than a short list of exemptions, rather than only from posts involving the exercise of public authority and safeguarding the general interests of the State.
exclusion_notes: Posts reserved for nationals in private companies belong to RI-FMW-001.
notes: Repeated annual finding; the screening report adds the test of case law of the Court of Justice.

label: Legal and organisational framework for joining EURES
definition: The country has not set up the legal and organisational arrangements needed to join the European network of employment services, such as a system for appointing EURES members and partners and access for private employment agencies.
exclusion_notes: Staff training and IT capacity of the employment service belong to RI-FMW-005; the European Labour Authority belongs to RI-FMW-006.
notes: Annual reports 2020 to 2025 report no preparatory steps, while the 2025 screening report rates EURES preparation as good; this tension should be checked at classification. Items on private employment agency access also carry TECH-INTEROP.

label: Employment service capacity for EURES and labour mobility
definition: The public employment service lacks trained staff or adequate IT and data systems to take part in EU labour mobility networks and vacancy exchange.
exclusion_notes: Legal designation of EURES members and partners belongs to RI-FMW-004; electronic exchange of social security data belongs to RI-FMW-010.
notes: Several 2025 screening items are positive findings (IT in place, capacity satisfactory); the open points are training updates after staff turnover and ESCO mapping. The technology agent may draft a related TEC issue on connection to EU systems.

label: Alignment with the European Labour Authority regulation
definition: National law is not aligned with the regulation establishing the European Labour Authority, including the arrangements for cooperating with it.
exclusion_notes: EURES participation belongs to RI-FMW-004; bodies supporting mobile workers' rights belong to RI-FMW-007.
notes: Small evidence base: two findings from one source, plus mentions in the composite employment service recommendation. Candidate for merging with RI-FMW-004 or RI-FMW-007.

label: Information and support for mobile workers on their rights
definition: There is no designated body supporting EU mobile workers in their rights and the system for informing them of their rights is weak.
exclusion_notes: The substance of the rights themselves belongs to RI-FMW-001 to RI-FMW-003.
notes: Small evidence base: three items from one source (2025 screening report), two of which split one sentence. Kept separate because it is a distinct acquis obligation another country could plausibly face.

label: Gaps in bilateral social security and healthcare agreements
definition: Bilateral social security coordination and healthcare agreements do not yet cover all EU Member States or all branches, so workers moving before accession lack coordinated protection.
exclusion_notes: Alignment of national social security law with the coordination regulations belongs to RI-FMW-009; the European Health Insurance Card belongs to RI-FMW-011.
notes: Repeated annual recommendation. The screening report credits this experience as giving a good level of preparation. MEC-01 fits loosely; see the mechanism proposal on missing agreements.

label: National social security law not aligned with the coordination regulations
definition: National pension, health and other social security laws are only partly aligned with the EU coordination regulations, for example through citizenship conditions, and the administrative measures for applying them at accession are not identified or in place.
exclusion_notes: Bilateral agreements belong to RI-FMW-008; electronic exchange of social security information belongs to RI-FMW-010.

label: Readiness for electronic exchange of social security information
definition: The institutions lack the IT and human capacity to exchange social security information electronically with Member States (the EESSI system) and to use electronic health insurance data.
exclusion_notes: Legal alignment of social security law belongs to RI-FMW-009; the healthcare access rights of EHIC holders belong to RI-FMW-011.
notes: Chapter 2 issue that materially concerns the technology theme. RI-TEC-031 merged into it at G4 (G4-D03).

label: Access to healthcare for EU citizens through the European Health Insurance Card
definition: EU citizens can use the European Health Insurance Card or access medical services only where a bilateral arrangement exists, so access is not yet available to citizens of all Member States.
exclusion_notes: Electronic use of EHIC data belongs to RI-FMW-010; general bilateral social security agreements belong to RI-FMW-008.
notes: Overlaps with RI-FMW-008, since access depends on bilateral agreements; candidate for merging. The 2025 screening report rates EHIC technical alignment as satisfactory.

label: Supplementary pension rights of mobile workers
definition: National law is not aligned with the EU directives on supplementary pension rights, such as the acquisition and preservation of rights for workers who move between Member States.
exclusion_notes: Statutory social security pensions belong to RI-FMW-009.
notes: Single source (2025 screening report). Equal treatment in voluntary funds is already provided, entering into force at accession.

label: Weak corruption prevention in the administration of worker mobility
definition: The bodies administering free movement of workers, notably the employment service, lack a specific integrity policy, internal controls and audit capacity to prevent corruption.
exclusion_notes: General anti-corruption policy outside free movement of workers belongs to Chapter 23 and is out of scope.
notes: Included because the Commission ties these measures specifically to Chapter 2 (run record boundary). Two generic statements on ministry capacity placed in the anti-corruption section are mapped here with a note.

label: Artificial intelligence framework not aligned or supported by structures
definition: The rules on artificial intelligence are not aligned with the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, or the enforcement structures and wider capacity needed to apply them and support trustworthy uptake are not in place.
exclusion_notes: General innovation support and business digital adoption without an artificial intelligence element belong to the business digital adoption issue.
notes: Small evidence base: one Commission recommendation (AI Act alignment and enforcement structures) and one welcome of an AI Factory Antenna. Kept as a separate issue because TECH-AI is an approved theme and the recommendation is material; the analyst may prefer to hold it until more evidence exists.

label: Digital transformation strategy and governance weak
definition: There is no adopted long-term strategy for digital transformation aligned with EU targets, or the ministry or agency responsible lacks the capacity, staff and inter-institutional coordination to lead and monitor it.
exclusion_notes: Cybersecurity strategies belong to the cybersecurity legal and strategic framework issue; broadband plans belong to the broadband planning issue; the delivery of specific e-services belongs to the e-services issue.
notes: Includes measurement of digital performance (Digital Economy and Society Index data, eGovernment benchmarking) and Commission assessments of the digital part of a reform plan. The analyst may wish to split strategy adoption from institutional capacity.

label: Limited range and use of transactional digital public services
definition: Few public services can be completed fully online through the national e-services portal, the most requested services are not available, and use of and satisfaction with the services that exist remain low, including for people with limited digital means.
exclusion_notes: Sector systems with their own issue (tax, procurement, point of single contact, eHealth, justice, customs) belong there; the underlying registers and data exchange that make services possible belong to the base registers and data exchange issues; electronic identification tools belong to the digital identity issues.
notes: Largest issue by item count. Many items are repeated in the annual report, the Economic Reform Programme assessment and policy guidance. The analyst may wish to split supply of services from uptake and inclusion. Test at G5 whether items can be assigned consistently; split only if not (G4-D05).

label: Core e-government building blocks missing
definition: Shared systems that every institution needs to work digitally, such as a single document management system, legal and technical arrangements for electronic archiving, a digital mailbox and shared administrative information systems, are missing or little used.
exclusion_notes: Data exchange between institutions through the interoperability platform belongs to the interoperability use issue; citizen-facing services belong to the e-services issue.
notes: Mostly Reform Agenda payment conditions and their assessment; small base of report findings.

label: Limited taxpayer e-services
definition: The tax administration offers a limited range of electronic services to taxpayers.
exclusion_notes: Connection to EU taxation IT systems belongs to the issue on other EU sectoral information systems; customs IT belongs to the customs issue. The integrated IT tax system and other back-office tax IT are out of the issue under R22, except where a quote also covers e-services.
notes: Recommendation repeated almost word for word every year from 2020 to 2026. Narrowed at G4 (G4-D04) to fit R22.

label: Electronic public procurement tools underused
definition: The electronic public procurement system works, but some of its modules, such as the e-marketplace for low-value contracts and e-catalogues, are incomplete or little used by contracting authorities, and its data are not yet used for red-flag analysis.
exclusion_notes: Wider public procurement reform without a digital element belongs to Chapter 5 issues outside this theme.
notes: Several items are positive findings (system functions efficiently).

label: Online access for service providers and regulated professions incomplete
definition: The point of single contact does not give service providers full online information and procedures as the Services Directive requires, and there is no transparent electronic register of regulated professions and qualifications.
exclusion_notes: General e-services for citizens belong to the e-services issue; connection to the Internal Market Information System belongs to the issue on other EU sectoral information systems.
notes: Combines the point of single contact and the register of regulated professions (both Chapter 3). The analyst may wish to split them.

label: Electronic public consultation platform underused
definition: The national electronic platform for consulting the public on draft laws is used for a small and falling share of draft laws, does not always hold final texts, and is little used by citizens and businesses.
exclusion_notes: Proactive publication of datasets belongs to the open data issue.
notes: Technology is the channel rather than the problem; the analyst may consider whether this issue meets the materiality test or belongs to public administration reform. Retired at G4 (G4-D02): no in-scope recommendation supports it.

label: eHealth systems not interoperable or aligned with EU rules
definition: Electronic health systems are not interoperable with health insurance data, referrals remain on paper, and the legislation is not aligned with the EU acquis on eHealth.
exclusion_notes: Health system funding and staffing without a digital element are outside this theme.

label: Justice system digitalisation incomplete
definition: Courts and justice bodies lack full electronic case handling, electronic communication with courts, videoconferencing and connected case management software, and judicial IT depends on donor funding.
exclusion_notes: Connection to EU justice and home affairs systems such as ECRIS belongs to that issue; interoperability for checking asset declarations belongs to the interoperability use issue.
notes: Several items flagged theme_doubtful. Recheck at G5 (G4-D08): court IT may be back-office under R22.

label: Electronic communications law not aligned with EU rules
definition: The law on electronic communications is not fully aligned with the European Electronic Communications Code, the Gigabit Infrastructure Act and related rules on cost reduction, spectrum, roaming and open internet access.
exclusion_notes: Regulator independence and funding belong to the regulator issue; security of 5G networks belongs to the 5G issue; ePrivacy belongs to the data protection legal issue.
notes: Includes roaming and net neutrality, where most findings are positive.

label: Electronic communications regulator independence and market oversight weak
definition: The electronic communications regulator lacks guaranteed independence in appointments and funding and sufficient capacity, and competitive safeguards in a concentrated telecom market are not applied.
exclusion_notes: Media regulators and public broadcasters (named in the same recommendation) are outside this theme; legal alignment of the law belongs to the electronic communications law issue.
notes: Combines regulator independence and competition; the analyst may wish to split them.

label: Broadband and high-capacity network coverage uneven
definition: Small businesses and rural or non-urban areas face obstacles to fixed broadband, and high-capacity and 5G networks are still being rolled out.
exclusion_notes: National planning, targets and funding instruments belong to the broadband planning issue; school connectivity under digital education is outside scope (R2).
notes: Many items are the same sentence repeated across reports.

label: Broadband planning and investment framework incomplete
definition: National broadband targets, plans and investment are not aligned with EU Digital Decade targets, and EU funding instruments, State aid rules and backhaul studies are not used or in place.
exclusion_notes: Coverage outcomes belong to the coverage issue.
notes: Small evidence base.

label: Base registers incomplete, unreliable or not digitalised
definition: Key registers, above all the population register, hold data of poor quality or are little used, and many institutional, property and intellectual property registers are not yet digitalised or kept up to date.
exclusion_notes: The exchange of register data between institutions belongs to the interoperability use issue; the register of regulated professions belongs to the online access issue.
notes: Property register items are mainly property rights issues flagged theme_doubtful.

label: Open data and re-use of public sector information incomplete
definition: Institutions do not regularly publish and update datasets on the open data portal, and legislation is only partly aligned with the Open Data Directive and related EU data rules.
exclusion_notes: General transparency and access to documents belong to public administration reform outside this theme.
notes: Includes alignment with the INSPIRE Directive on spatial data, where the Commission's findings are positive.

label: Personal data protection law not aligned with EU rules
definition: The personal data protection framework is not fully aligned with the General Data Protection Regulation, the Law Enforcement Directive and the ePrivacy Directive, rules on international transfers are missing, and sector laws are not harmonised.
exclusion_notes: Whether the authority is consulted on draft laws belongs to the advice issue; compliance in practice belongs to the compliance issue.

label: Data protection authority lacks independence and resources
definition: The data protection supervisory authority depends on government for staffing and funding, has capacity below its tasks, and can be left without a director.
exclusion_notes: Whether the authority's advice is followed belongs to the advice issue.

label: Data protection authority not consulted and its advice not followed
definition: The data protection authority is not systematically consulted on sector and implementing laws, its recommendations are often not implemented, and parliament does not follow up its reports.
exclusion_notes: Independence and resources belong to the authority issue; electoral data processing belongs to the electoral issue.

label: Weak compliance with data protection rules
definition: Data controllers, including public bodies, do not apply data protection law in practice, breaches are frequent and not always reported, awareness is low, and sanctions are rare.
exclusion_notes: Gaps in the law itself belong to the legal alignment issue; electoral processing belongs to the electoral issue.

label: Personal data protection in electoral processes weak
definition: The processing of personal data in elections, including biometric data and campaign use, lacks oversight and was introduced without assessing compliance or consulting the data protection authority.
exclusion_notes: Voter register data quality belongs to the base registers issue.

label: Cybersecurity legal and strategic framework incomplete
definition: Network and information security law is not fully aligned with the NIS2 Directive and the Cybersecurity Act, the national cybersecurity strategy is late or fragmented in implementation, and responsibilities are split without effective coordination.
exclusion_notes: Staffing and operational capacity of incident response teams belong to the operational capacity issue; 5G security belongs to the 5G issue; cybercrime law enforcement is outside this theme.
notes: Combines legal alignment and strategy, as the EU usually requires them together. The analyst may wish to split strategy and coordination.

label: Operational cybersecurity capacity of public institutions weak
definition: The national incident response centre and state institutions lack staff, expertise and secure infrastructure, so government services and digital infrastructure remain exposed to attacks.
exclusion_notes: Legal and strategic gaps belong to the legal and strategic framework issue; hybrid threats and disinformation without a cybersecurity element are outside this theme.

label: Security of 5G networks not ensured
definition: The EU 5G Cybersecurity Toolbox, including supplier risk assessment and restrictions on high-risk suppliers, is not fully transposed or applied when 5G networks are deployed.
exclusion_notes: 5G coverage and spectrum assignment belong to the coverage and electronic communications law issues.

label: Electronic identification and trust services law not aligned
definition: The law on electronic identification and trust services is not fully aligned with eIDAS and the European Digital Identity Regulation, including the Digital Identity Wallet, and implementing rules are pending.
exclusion_notes: Whether eID and trust services work in practice or are recognised by the EU belongs to the provision and recognition issue.

label: Electronic identification and trust services not usable or recognised
definition: Electronic identification and signature tools are costly, cumbersome and little used, qualified trust services are not widely available, and the country is not yet on the EU trusted list or in cross-border wallet arrangements.
exclusion_notes: Legal alignment belongs to the law issue.

label: Interoperability framework not aligned with EU
definition: The national interoperability framework is not aligned with the latest European Interoperability Framework or the Interoperable Europe Act.
exclusion_notes: Actual use of the interoperability platform belongs to the interoperability use issue.
notes: Many items are duplicates across two copies of the same 2023 assessment.

label: Interoperability platform and data exchange underused
definition: Institutions do not use the national interoperability platform regularly, so administrative data are not shared ex officio between institutions, including for checks such as asset declarations and inspections.
exclusion_notes: The framework's alignment with EU texts belongs to the framework issue; register data quality belongs to the base registers issue.
notes: Several asset declaration items are flagged theme_doubtful but fit.

label: Customs IT systems not aligned with EU electronic customs
definition: National customs IT systems are not yet aligned with the EU electronic customs strategic plan, and upgrades such as the New Computerised Transit System phases, export and import control systems are delayed or understaffed.
exclusion_notes: Tax administration IT belongs to the tax issue.
notes: Customs IT upgrades are incidental under TECH-INTEROP unless they concern connection to EU systems; all mapped items concern alignment with EU customs systems.

label: Not ready for EU justice, home affairs and border information systems
definition: The country lacks the systems, technical adaptations and funding to connect to EU justice and home affairs systems such as ECRIS, the Visa Information System and Eurodac.
exclusion_notes: Domestic judicial digitalisation belongs to the justice issue.
notes: Items come from the screening reports (two copies).

label: Electronic exchange of social security and employment data with the EU not ready
definition: The country is at an early stage in preparing for the electronic exchange of social security information (EESSI) and the European Health Insurance Card, while EURES IT is largely in place but not open to all providers.
exclusion_notes: Chapter 2 rights and coordination of social security without an electronic exchange element belong to Chapter 2 issues.
notes: Chapter 2 items, also drafted as Chapter 2 issues by another agent; the analyst should decide whether to keep both mappings. Merged at G4 (G4-D03): all its items are also under Chapter 2 issues; EURES IT items stay under RI-FMW-005.

label: Not ready to connect to other EU sectoral information systems
definition: Systems in other sectors are not yet ready to interconnect with EU information systems, such as the business registers interconnection system, the Internal Market Information System, the civil protection system, EU taxation systems and the own resources reporting system.
exclusion_notes: Customs, justice and home affairs, and social security systems have their own issues.
notes: Residual issue grouping many sectors with one or two items each; the analyst may wish to split it by sector later.

label: Low digital adoption by businesses
definition: Digitalisation of the economy and adoption of digital technologies by small businesses remain low compared with the EU and undermine competitiveness, and EU programmes and digital innovation hubs are little used.
exclusion_notes: Rules for the digital single market belong to the digital single market issue; digital skills are outside scope unless linked to an in-scope recommendation (R2).
notes: Mostly generic findings repeated in economic governance documents; few specific recommendations.

label: Digital single market rules not aligned
definition: Legislation is not aligned with EU rules on online platforms and services, such as the Digital Services Act, the Digital Markets Act, the platform-to-business and geo-blocking regulations, and e-commerce is developing slowly.
exclusion_notes: Company law digital tools belong to the company law issue; consumer contract rules for digital content are outside this theme.

label: Digital tools in company law not fully aligned
definition: Company law is not fully aligned with EU rules on the use of digital tools and processes, such as online formation, electronic filing and director checks.
exclusion_notes: Interconnection with the business registers interconnection system belongs to the issue on other EU sectoral information systems.
notes: Later findings report high alignment.
